declarations.name: Causal.symmRationalLine_separates_locallyStronglyCausal
declarations.notes: Conjuncts 1-22 are, in order and verbatim, those of Causal.symmRationalLine_separates_futureOneConnected (Causal/FutureOneConnectedVacuous.lean:330-343), rebuilt from it by destructuring (kb/0276). Conjunct 24, 'forall W p, p in W -> not StronglyCausalOn W', is the target's 'no point has a strongly causal open neighbourhood', and is stronger than 23. declarations.name: Causal.symmRationalLine_not_stronglyCausalOn
declarations.notes: Correct and not vacuous: p in W rules out W = bottom, where StronglyCausalOn holds vacuously, and the proof uses DiamondConfinement's definition (:371) directly. With Ioo l u inside W about p and m = (p+u)/2, it asks for a V in nhds p inside Ioo l m, causally convex in W. It takes a rational r in V and a rational r' in (m, u). Then uIcc r r' lies in Ioo l u, which lies in W, so r <=_W r' <=_W r, r' is in diamond W r r, and so r' is in V, which is inside Ioo l m: a contradiction. This is the ladder's argument, run with (l, u) for (p - eps, p + eps).

The new conjuncts are: forall W AbsolutelyMinimalOn W at position 4, the 'may join' of the target; FutureOneConnected and forall W FutureOneConnectedOn W (13-14, since lt is empty); LocallyStronglyCausal (15); not CausallyPlain and not HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere (20-21, lt empty, on a non-empty space). declarations.name: Causal.loopFan_locallyStronglyCausal
declarations.notes: Sound. Box lemma (:223): along a tent, x = eps_n(1 - 2t) is decreasing, so a parameter between two parameters with x in (a, b) has x in (a, b). The height is unimodal, so it is at least the smaller end height, which is > c. It is at most the larger end height on one side of the top. Across the top (s < 1/2 < t), the piece in W puts the top in W, and hcross gives top < d. Applications: (1) loopLow (height < 1, kappa = 1 - q.2): no top is in it, since a top has height 1 + eps_n > 1, so hcross is vacuous. (2) loopSide (x != 0, kappa = |q.1|): no top is in it, since a top has x = 0. (3) loopCap n, the band (1 + eps_{n+1}, 1 + 2eps_n - eps_{n+1}): the only top in it is gamma_n's (loopPeak_mem_cap_iff, with combEps_two_mul_sub_le for m < n and strict antitonicity for m > n; checked by hand: (n+3)n <= (n+1)(n+2)). A box about that top has ceiling 1 + eps_n + delta. A box about a point with x != 0 of half-width at most |x| lies on one side of x = 0 and cannot hold gamma_m(s) and gamma_m(t) with s < 1/2 < t (x > 0 at one, < 0 at the other), so hcross holds by exfalso. The cover is complete: a point with x = 0 is a (in loopLow; loopSet_cases) or a top (eq_half_of_loopGamma_fst), and every other point is in loopSide. loopFan_stronglyCausalOn_of_boxes (:262) turns 'small centred boxes convex in W' into StronglyCausalOn W through the subtype sup metric. Not vacuous: StronglyCausalOn top <-> StronglyCausal fails for loopFan (conjunct 16), and the module shows loopLow, a neighbourhood of a, is strongly causal as a spacetime although M is not strongly causal at a (:437).

findings.what: The docstring of loopFan_causallyConvexIn_box states its hypothesis for 'every piece of a tent inside W that passes the top of its tent, with both ends in the box'. The Lean hypothesis hcross (:225-226) is stronger. It quantifies over every n and every s < 1/2 < t with only the top loopγ n (1/2) in W and both ends in the box, without asking the piece γ_n[s, t] to lie in W. So the docstring describes a stronger lemma than the one proved. The three applications satisfy the stronger hypothesis, so no main result is affected.
findings.fix: Either reword the docstrings ('once every tent whose top lies in W, with a point on each side of its top in the box, has that top below the box's ceiling'), or weaken hcross to take (∀ ρ ∈ Icc s t, loopγ n ρ ∈ W) instead of loopγ n (1 / 2) ∈ W and pass hW at :258. The three applications then derive the top's membership from it.
